Add store accessors to Event model for capturing old/new values of changed fields.

## File to Modify
`app/models/event/particulars.rb`

## Changes Required
Update store_accessor line to include new fields:
```ruby
store_accessor :particulars,
  :beads_issue_id,       # Existing
  :old_status,           # New - previous status value
  :new_status,           # New - current status value
  :old_assignee,         # New - previous assignee email
  :new_assignee,         # New - current assignee email
  :old_title,            # New - previous title text
  :new_title,            # New - current title text
```

Write comprehensive tests for ChangeDetector
description:
Create thorough test coverage for change detection logic covering all field types and edge cases.

## File to Create
`test/services/beads/change_detector_test.rb`

## Test Cases Required

**Status changes**:
- open → in_progress → returns StatusChange
- in_progress → closed → returns StatusChange  
- closed → open → returns StatusChange (reopened)
- open → open (no change) → returns empty array

**Assignment changes**:
- nil → email → returns AssignmentChange
- email → nil → returns AssignmentChange (unassigned)
- email → different email → returns AssignmentChange
- email → same email (no change) → returns empty array

**Comment additions**:
- 0 comments → 1 comment → returns CommentAddition
- 1 comment → 2 comments → returns one CommentAddition
- Same comments → returns empty array
- Comments reordered (same fingerprints) → returns empty array

**Title/description/priority changes**:
- String/number changes → returns appropriate change object
- Whitespace-only changes → should detect (or ignore based on decision)
- Empty → non-empty → returns change
- No change → returns empty array

**Multiple changes**:
- Status + assignment both change → returns both StatusChange and AssignmentChange
- All fields change → returns all change objects
- Order: status first, then assignment, then comments (predictable)

**Edge cases**:
- Empty old_state (first mutation) → all fields are 'additions', handle gracefully
- Nil values in old state
- Missing keys in hashes
- Malformed comment data

## Test Structure Example
```ruby
class Beads::ChangeDetectorTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "detects status change from open to closed" do
    old_state = { status: "open", title: "Bug" }
    new_state = { status: "closed", title: "Bug" }

    changes = Beads::ChangeDetector.new(old_state, new_state).changes

    assert_equal 1, changes.size
    assert_instance_of Beads::Changes::StatusChange, changes.first
    assert_equal "open", changes.first.from
    assert_equal "closed", changes.first.to
  end

  test "detects multiple changes in single mutation" do
    old_state = { status: "open", assignee: nil, title: "Bug" }
    new_state = { status: "in_progress", assignee: "bob@example.com", title: "Fix bug" }

    changes = Beads::ChangeDetector.new(old_state, new_state).changes

    assert_equal 3, changes.size
    change_types = changes.map(&:class).map(&:name)
    assert_includes change_types, "Beads::Changes::StatusChange"
    assert_includes change_types, "Beads::Changes::AssignmentChange"
    assert_includes change_types, "Beads::Changes::TitleChange"
  end
end
```

## Coverage Target
Minimum 15 test cases covering:
- Each change type (7 types × 2 tests each = 14)
- Multiple changes (1 test)
- Edge cases (as discovered)

Run: `bin/rails test test/services/beads/change_detector_test.rb`

title: Handle beads API errors in event processing
description:
Add robust error handling for beads daemon failures during mutation processing and event creation.

## Files to Modify
`app/services/beads_bridge.rb`
`app/models/event.rb`

## Current Problem
If beads daemon is down or issue deleted:
- `fetch_issue` raises BeadsClient::Error
- `event.eventable` tries to fetch and fails
- Timeline rendering breaks

## Solutions

### BeadsBridge Error Handling

Wrap mutation processing:
```ruby
def process_mutation(mutation)
  issue_id = mutation["IssueID"]
  
  begin
    issue = fetch_issue(issue_id)
  rescue BeadsClient::Error => e
    Rails.logger.warn("BeadsBridge: Cannot fetch issue \#{issue_id}: \#{e.message}")
    # For delete mutations, this is expected
    return handle_delete(issue_id) if mutation["Type"] == "delete"
    # For others, skip this mutation
    return
  end

  return unless issue

  case mutation["Type"]
  when "create" then handle_create(issue)
```

### Event.eventable Error Handling

Current code in `app/models/event.rb:59`:

### State Cache Error Handling

In handle_update, if cache parsing fails:

```ruby
  state = BeadsIssueState.find_by(board_id: board.id, issue_id: issue.id)

  if state.nil?
    Rails.logger.info("BeadsBridge: No cache for \#{issue.id}, treating as create")

    previous_snapshot = state.parsed_snapshot

  end
```

## Error Scenarios

| Error | Cause | Handling |
|-------|-------|----------|
| BeadsClient::DaemonNotRunningError | Daemon stopped | Skip poll cycle (logged) |
| BeadsClient::Error (issue not found) | Issue deleted | Skip mutation or handle as delete |
| JSON::ParserError | Corrupted cache | Rebuild cache entry |
| ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid | Event validation failed | Log error, continue processing |
| StandardError | Unexpected error | Log with full trace, continue |

- **warn**: Expected conditions (daemon down, issue not found)
- **error**: Unexpected failures (corrupt cache, event creation failure)
- **info**: Normal operations (cache rebuild, first-time create)
- **debug**: Verbose details (creator lookup, change detection)

```ruby
namespace :beads do
```

title: Integrate ChangeDetector into BeadsBridge
description:
Update BeadsBridge mutation processing to use state cache and ChangeDetector for creating rich events.

## Files to Modify
`app/services/beads_bridge.rb`

## Current Behavior (line ~43)
```ruby
def process_mutation(mutation)
  issue_id = mutation["IssueID"]

  case mutation["Type"]
  when "create"
    broadcast_card_created(issue_id)
    create_event_for_creation(issue_id)
  when "update"
    broadcast_card_moved(issue_id)
    # No events created
  when "close", "delete"
    broadcast_card_removed(issue_id)
    create_event_for_closure(issue_id) if mutation["Type"] == "close"
  end
end
```

## New Behavior
Replace `process_mutation` method with:
```ruby
def process_mutation(mutation)
  issue_id = mutation["IssueID"]
  issue = fetch_issue(issue_id)
  return unless issue  # Skip if can't fetch

  case mutation["Type"]
  when "create"
    handle_create(issue)
  when "update"
    handle_update(issue)
  when "delete"
    handle_delete(issue_id)
  end
end
```

## Implementation Details

**handle_create method** (add to private section):
```ruby
def handle_create(issue)
  # Serialize BeadsIssue to hash for storage
  issue_data = serialize_issue(issue)

  # Store initial state in cache
  BeadsIssueState.upsert(
    {
      board_id: board.id,
      issue_id: issue.id,
      snapshot: issue_data.to_json,
      synced_at: Time.current
    },
    unique_by: [:board_id, :issue_id]
  )

  # Create published event
  create_event_for_creation(issue)

  # Broadcast to UI
  broadcast_card_created(issue.id)
end
```

**handle_update method** (add to private section):
```ruby
def handle_update(issue)
  # Load previous state from cache
  state = BeadsIssueState.find_by(board_id: board.id, issue_id: issue.id)

  # No previous state: treat as first-time create
  if state.nil?
    Rails.logger.info("BeadsBridge: No cached state for #{issue.id}, treating as create")
    return handle_create(issue)
  end

  # Compare states
  previous_snapshot = state.parsed_snapshot
  current_snapshot = serialize_issue(issue)

  detector = Beads::ChangeDetector.new(previous_snapshot, current_snapshot)
  changes = detector.changes

  # Create event for each semantic change
  changes.each do |change|
    create_event_for_change(issue, change)
  end

  # Update cached state
  state.update_snapshot\!(current_snapshot)

  # Broadcast UI updates (handles column moves)
  broadcast_card_moved(issue.id) if changes.any?
end
```

**handle_delete method** (add to private section):
```ruby
def handle_delete(issue_id)
  # Remove from state cache
  BeadsIssueState.where(board_id: board.id, issue_id: issue_id).destroy_all

  # Broadcast removal
  broadcast_card_removed(issue_id)

  # Note: Don't delete events (preserve history)
end
```

**serialize_issue helper** (CRITICAL - BeadsIssue is not ActiveRecord):
```ruby
def serialize_issue(beads_issue)
  # BeadsIssue doesn't have .attributes like ActiveRecord
  # Extract relevant fields manually
  {
    id: beads_issue.id,
    title: beads_issue.title,
    description: beads_issue.description,
    status: beads_issue.status,
    priority: beads_issue.priority,
    issue_type: beads_issue.issue_type,
    assignee: beads_issue.assignee,
    labels: beads_issue.labels,
    comments: beads_issue.comments,
    created_at: beads_issue.created_at&.iso8601,
    updated_at: beads_issue.updated_at&.iso8601,
    closed_at: beads_issue.closed_at&.iso8601
  }
end
```

**create_event_for_change method** (replace existing):
```ruby
def create_event_for_change(issue, change)
  creator = find_creator_for_change(change) || beads_system_user

  Event.create\!(
    board: board,
    creator: creator,
    eventable_type: "BeadsIssue",
    eventable_id: uuid_for_issue(issue.id),
    action: change.event_action,
    beads_issue_id: issue.id,
    **change.event_particulars
  )
rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
  Rails.logger.error("BeadsBridge: Failed to create event for #{issue.id}: #{e.message}")
end
```

**find_creator_for_change method** (add to private):
```ruby
def find_creator_for_change(change)
  email = change.actor_email
  return nil unless email.present?

  identity = Identity.find_by(email_address: email)
  return nil unless identity

  user = identity.users.find_by(account: board.account)

  unless user
    Rails.logger.debug("BeadsBridge: No Fizzy user found for #{email} in account #{board.account.id}")
  end

  user
end

def beads_system_user
  @beads_system_user ||= begin
    identity = Identity.find_by(email_address: "hi@fizzybeads.com")
    identity&.users&.find_by(account: board.account)
  end
end
```

## Edge Cases Handled
- **No cached state on update**: Treat as create (backfill cache)
- **Multiple changes in one mutation**: Create multiple events (one per change)
- **Empty changes array**: No events created, just update cache
- **Creator lookup fails**: Fall back to Beads system user
- **Issue fetch fails**: Skip mutation processing entirely (return early)

## What Gets Removed
Delete these existing methods (replaced by handle_* methods):
- `create_event_for_creation`
- `create_event_for_update`  
- `create_event_for_closure`

Keep these:
- `fetch_issue`
- `broadcast_card_created/moved/removed`
- `find_column_for_issue`
- `update_timestamp`
- `uuid_for_issue`

title: Implement Beads::ChangeDetector service
description:
Create service that compares old and new beads issue states and returns semantic change objects.

## File to Create
`app/services/beads/change_detector.rb`

## Full Implementation
```ruby
module Beads
  class ChangeDetector
    def initialize(old_state, new_state)
      @old = (old_state || {}).deep_symbolize_keys
      @new = new_state.deep_symbolize_keys
    end

    def changes
      [
        status_change,
        assignment_change,
        title_change,
        description_change,
        priority_change,
        labels_change,
        *comment_additions
      ].compact
    end

    private

    def status_change
      return nil if @old[:status] == @new[:status]
      
      Changes::StatusChange.new(
        from: @old[:status],
        to: @new[:status],
        actor: @new[:assignee]  # Assume assignee made the change
      )
    end

    def assignment_change
      return nil if @old[:assignee] == @new[:assignee]
      
      Changes::AssignmentChange.new(
        from: @old[:assignee],
        to: @new[:assignee]
      )
    end

    def title_change
      old_title = @old[:title].to_s.strip
      new_title = @new[:title].to_s.strip
      return nil if old_title == new_title
      
      Changes::TitleChange.new(from: @old[:title], to: @new[:title])
    end

    def description_change
      old_desc = @old[:description].to_s.strip
      new_desc = @new[:description].to_s.strip
      return nil if old_desc == new_desc
      
      Changes::DescriptionChange.new(from: @old[:description], to: @new[:description])
    end

    def priority_change
      return nil if @old[:priority] == @new[:priority]
      
      Changes::PriorityChange.new(
        from: @old[:priority],
        to: @new[:priority]
      )
    end

    def labels_change
      old_labels = (@old[:labels] || []).sort
      new_labels = (@new[:labels] || []).sort
      return nil if old_labels == new_labels

      added = new_labels - old_labels
      removed = old_labels - new_labels
      return nil if added.empty? && removed.empty?

      Changes::LabelsChange.new(added: added, removed: removed)
    end

    def comment_additions
      old_comments = @old[:comments] || []
      new_comments = @new[:comments] || []

      # Build fingerprint sets for comparison
      old_fps = old_comments.map { |c| fingerprint(c) }.to_set
      new_fps = new_comments.map { |c| fingerprint(c) }.to_set

      # Find new fingerprints
      added_fps = new_fps - old_fps

      # Map back to comment objects
      added_fps.map do |fp|
        comment = new_comments.find { |c| fingerprint(c) == fp }
        Changes::CommentAddition.new(comment)
      end
    end

    def fingerprint(comment)
      # Unique ID: author email + creation timestamp
      # Assumes comments are immutable (can't edit)
      c = comment.deep_symbolize_keys
      "\#{c[:author]}-\#{c[:created_at]}"
    end
  end
end
```

## Field Comparison Strategy

**String fields** (title, description):
- Strip whitespace before comparing
- Empty string and nil considered different (preserve semantics)

**Scalar fields** (status, assignee, priority):
- Direct equality comparison
- nil is a valid value (different from empty string)

**Array fields** (labels, comments):
- Sort before comparison for labels (order doesn't matter)
- Order DOES matter for comments (chronological)
- Use set operations to find additions/removals

**Nested objects** (comments):
- Use fingerprinting for identity (author + timestamp)
- Assumes comments are immutable (no edits, only additions)

## Comment Fingerprinting

Why `author + created_at`:
- Beads doesn't provide comment IDs
- Author alone not unique (same person can comment twice)
- Timestamp alone not unique (multiple comments at same second possible but rare)
- Combined = reliable unique identifier

Limitation:
- If beads allows comment editing, fingerprint won't detect edits
- Acceptable trade-off: edits are rare, additions are common

## Empty Old State Handling

When `old_state` is nil or empty (first mutation):
- `@old` becomes `{}`
- All field comparisons treat missing keys as nil
- Every non-nil field in new state = a change
- Example: First update mutation treats like create (all fields new)

title: Create beads_issue_states table migration
description:
Create database migration and model for caching beads issue state snapshots.

## File to Create
`db/migrate/XXXXXX_create_beads_issue_states.rb`

## Migration Code
```ruby
create_table :beads_issue_states, id: :uuid do |t|
  t.references :board, null: false, type: :uuid, foreign_key: true
  t.string :issue_id, null: false  # 'fizzy-abc', 'roboco-123'
  t.text :snapshot, null: false    # JSON string of full issue data
  t.datetime :synced_at, null: false

  t.timestamps

  t.index [:board_id, :issue_id], unique: true
end
```

## Model Code
`app/models/beads_issue_state.rb`:
```ruby
class BeadsIssueState < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :board

  validates :issue_id, presence: true, uniqueness: { scope: :board_id }
  validates :snapshot, presence: true
  validates :synced_at, presence: true

  scope :for_issue, ->(board, issue_id) { where(board: board, issue_id: issue_id) }

  # Parse snapshot JSON when reading
  def parsed_snapshot
    @parsed_snapshot ||= JSON.parse(snapshot).deep_symbolize_keys
  rescue JSON::ParserError => e
    Rails.logger.error("BeadsIssueState: Invalid JSON in snapshot for issue #{issue_id}: #{e.message}")
    {}
  end

  # Update with new snapshot data
  def update_snapshot!(issue_data_hash)
    update!(
      snapshot: issue_data_hash.to_json,
      synced_at: Time.current
    )
  end
end
```

## Storage Format
**CRITICAL**: Snapshot stored as JSON STRING (text column), not parsed hash.

Why:
- BeadsIssue attributes are hash, not ActiveRecord
- Need to serialize: `issue_data_hash.to_json` → store
- Need to deserialize: `JSON.parse(snapshot)` → compare

Example snapshot content:
```json
{
  "id": "fizzy-abc",
  "title": "Fix bug",
  "status": "open",
  "assignee": null,
  "comments": [],
  "created_at": "2025-12-04T12:00:00Z"
}
```

## Initial Population Strategy
When first connecting a board with existing issues:
- Mutations will be 'update' type with no cached state
- BeadsBridge should detect missing cache and treat as 'create'
- This backfills cache during first poll cycle

Migration doesn't pre-populate - cache builds organically as mutations processed.

## Test After Creation
```bash
bin/rails db:migrate

# Test creation
bin/rails runner "
  data = { id: 'test-123', title: 'Test', status: 'open' }
  state = BeadsIssueState.create!(
    board: Board.first,

    snapshot: data.to_json,
    synced_at: Time.current
  )
  puts 'Created state: ' + state.id
  puts 'Parsed snapshot: ' + state.parsed_snapshot.inspect
  puts '✓ Table works correctly'
"
```

title: State Cache & Change Detection Infrastructure
description:
Build foundation for detecting what changed in beads issue updates by maintaining a state cache and implementing semantic change detection.

## Goal
Enable accurate change detection from beads mutation API's generic 'update' events by caching previous issue states and comparing to current states.

## Architecture

**State Cache Table**: `beads_issue_states`
- Stores last known state snapshot (JSON) per issue
- Single source of truth for 'what we last saw'
- Enables efficient comparison without multiple RPC calls

**ChangeDetector Service**: `Beads::ChangeDetector`
- Compares old vs new issue states
- Returns semantic change objects (StatusChange, AssignmentChange, CommentAddition, etc.)
- Encapsulates comparison logic for testability

**Change Objects**: Value objects representing semantic changes
- Each knows: what changed, old/new values, event action, notification rules
- Examples: StatusChange, AssignmentChange, TitleChange, CommentAddition

## Why This Matters
Beads mutation API only tells us 'issue updated', not WHAT changed. Without state cache, we can't tell if an update was:
- Status changed open → closed (needs 'Done' event)
- Comment added (needs notification)
- Minor label change (no event needed)

## Technical Approach

Cache lifecycle:
1. First mutation: Store initial state
2. Update mutation: Load previous state → compare → detect changes → update cache
3. Delete mutation: Remove cache entry

Change detection:
1. Compare cached snapshot vs current issue data
2. Field-by-field comparison (status, assignee, title, comments, etc.)
3. Return array of Change objects representing semantic differences

## Success Criteria
- State cache populated for all beads issues across all boards
- ChangeDetector correctly identifies all change types
- Change objects provide correct event actions and particulars
- Foundation ready for rich event creation (next epic)

```ruby
  # Pattern from CardEventNotifier

    .where(role: [:owner, :admin, :member])
```

## Goal
External integrations can subscribe to beads events and receive HTTP POST webhooks when beads issues are created, updated, assigned, commented on, or closed.

**Webhook Action Permissions**: Extend PERMITTED_ACTIONS
- Add all `beads_issue_*` and `beads_comment_*` actions
- Allow webhook subscribers to choose which actions they care about

**Webhook Payload Rendering**: Update event template

- Support multiple formats (JSON, Slack mrkdwn, Campfire HTML)

```json
    "action": "beads_issue_closed",
    "timestamp": "2025-12-04T12:00:00Z",
    "board": {
```

## Current Code (line ~8)
```ruby
def self.for(source)
  case source
  when Event
    \"Notifier::\#{source.eventable.class}EventNotifier\".safe_constantize&.new(source)
  when Mention

end
```

## Current State
The home/events view shows activity timeline with 3 columns (Added/Updated/Done), but only for regular Fizzy cards. BeadsIssue activity is not tracked.

## Goal
Beads card actions (created, status changed, assigned, commented, etc.) should appear in the activity timeline alongside regular Fizzy cards, sorted by time.

## Parent Epic
This is part of fizzy-dz6 (Real-Time Bridge) epic. The mutation polling infrastructure built for real-time sync can also create Events for historical tracking.

## Implementation Approach (See Design Notes)
Use beads mutations API to create real Fizzy Event records. Same background job that polls mutations for real-time sync can also create Events for the activity timeline.

**Why this approach**:
- Reuses mutation polling infrastructure from parent epic
- Creates real Events → full Fizzy feature compatibility (webhooks, notifications, system comments)
- Reliable change detection without custom tracking
- Clean separation: beads owns data, Fizzy creates events from change feed

## See Design Notes
Run: bd show fizzy-ihi --design

Design notes contain full analysis of Fizzy's Event system and detailed implementation plan.
design:
## Current Understanding

Fizzy's activity timeline shows Events grouped by day into 3 columns (Added/Updated/Done). Events are created when cards change state, are assigned, commented on, etc. The timeline queries Events from the database and filters by TIMELINEABLE_ACTIONS.

**Problem**: BeadsIssue is not a database model - it's a value object wrapping beads RPC responses. Beads changes happen in git/JSONL, not in Fizzy's database, so no Events are created.

## Implementation Approaches

### Option 1: Real Events (Recommended)
Create actual Event records in Fizzy's database for beads card actions.

**Pros**:
- Full integration with Fizzy's system (webhooks, notifications, system comments)
- Persistent activity history
- Works with existing timeline views
- Enables filtering, searching across beads activity

**Cons**:
- Need to track when beads issues change (polling mutations?)
- Complexity of syncing beads → Fizzy events
- Potential for duplicate/missed events

**Implementation**:
1. Add BeadsIssue to eventable_type enum
2. Create events when beads actions occur (status change, assignment, etc.)
3. Implement event description logic for beads actions
4. Create event display partials for beads events
5. Poll beads mutations and create Events for changes

### Option 2: Virtual Events (Simpler)
Create BeadsEvent value objects that duck-type Event, merge with real Events in timeline.

**Pros**:
- Simpler - no database persistence needed
- Can query beads directly for recent activity
- No sync/polling complexity

**Cons**:
- No webhooks, notifications, or system comments for beads activity
- Can't filter/search beads events in Fizzy
- Timeline queries become more complex (merge two data sources)

**Implementation**:
1. Create BeadsEvent value object
2. Modify User::DayTimeline to fetch beads activity for the day
3. Merge beads events with regular events, sort by time
4. Create display partials for beads events

### Option 3: Hybrid (Best of Both)
Use beads mutations API to detect changes and create real Events.

**Pros**:
- Real Events for full integration
- Beads mutations API provides reliable change feed
- Can be background job driven (no polling in requests)

**Cons**:
- Need mutation polling background job
- Slightly more complex setup

**Implementation**:
1. Background job polls `beads_client.get_mutations(since: last_sync_time)`
2. For each mutation, create corresponding Event in Fizzy
3. Store last mutation timestamp in Board or Account
4. Events flow through normal Fizzy system

## Recommended Approach: Option 3 (Hybrid)

Use beads mutations API with a background poller to create real Events.

**Why**:
- Beads provides `get_mutations(since:)` specifically for this use case
- Real Events = full Fizzy feature compatibility
- Background job keeps request performance fast
- Reliable change detection without custom tracking

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Basic Event Creation
1. Add "BeadsIssue" to Event eventable_type (may need enum or polymorphic handling)
2. Create helper method `BeadsIssue#track_event_for_action(action, creator, **particulars)`
3. Map beads mutations to Fizzy event actions:
   - Mutation: status_changed → Event: beads_issue_status_changed
   - Mutation: assigned → Event: beads_issue_assigned
   - Mutation: created → Event: beads_issue_published
   - etc.

### Phase 2: Mutation Polling
1. Create `BeadsMutationPoller` background job (Solid Queue)
2. Store `last_mutation_timestamp` on Board model
3. Poll each beads board's mutations every 30-60 seconds
4. Create Events for each mutation
5. Update last_mutation_timestamp

### Phase 3: Event Display
1. Add beads event actions to TIMELINEABLE_ACTIONS
2. Extend Event::Description with beads action descriptions
3. Create event display partials in views/events/event/eventable/
4. Test timeline rendering with mixed Card and BeadsIssue events

### Phase 4: Polish
1. Handle edge cases (board deletion, beads repo unavailable)
2. Add manual "Sync Activity" button for immediate refresh
3. Optimize mutation queries (limit to recent activity window)
4. Add tests

## Open Questions

1. Should we create Events for ALL beads mutations or just user-facing ones?
2. How far back should we sync mutations on first setup?
3. Should mutation polling be per-board or account-wide?
4. What happens to Events if a beads issue is deleted from git?

## Files to Create/Modify

**New Files**:
- `app/jobs/beads_mutation_poller_job.rb`
- `app/models/beads_issue/eventable.rb` (concern)
- `app/views/events/event/eventable/_beads_issue_*.html.erb` (partials)

**Modified Files**:

- `app/models/event/description.rb` - Add beads action descriptions
- `app/models/user/day_timeline.rb` - Add beads actions to TIMELINEABLE_ACTIONS
- `app/models/board.rb` - Add last_mutation_timestamp column
- `config/recurring.yml` - Add mutation poller job

## Estimated Scope

Medium-Large task. Core functionality is ~3-4 hours, testing and polish another 2-3 hours.

title: Beads Issue Notification System
description:
Integrate beads issue events with Fizzy's notification system so users receive email, push, and in-app notifications for assignments, comments, and status changes.

## Goal
Users get notified when beads issues are assigned to them, commented on, or have significant status changes - using Fizzy's existing notification infrastructure (email bundling, push notifications, in-app).

## Architecture

**BeadsIssueEventNotifier**: Implements Fizzy's Notifier interface
- Recipient logic per action type (assigned → notify assignee, comment → notify watchers)
- Email → Identity → User mapping (beads emails to Fizzy users)
- Graceful handling when email doesn't match any Fizzy user

**Notifier.for enhancement**: Route BeadsIssue events to new notifier
- Detect `eventable_type == 'BeadsIssue'`
- Instantiate BeadsIssueEventNotifier

**Notification views**: Render beads events in notification UI
- Partial for BeadsIssue notifications
- Format with issue title, action description, timestamp

**Push notification support**: Update NotificationPusher
- Add payload formatting for beads actions
- Deep link URLs to issue detail pages

## Email Mapping Strategy

Beads uses emails (e.g., `alice@example.com`), Fizzy uses User accounts.

**Mapping flow**:
1. Event has `new_assignee: 'alice@example.com'` in particulars
2. Look up Identity by email: `Identity.find_by(email_address: 'alice@example.com')`
3. Find User in current account: `identity.users.find_by(account: board.account)`
4. If found: Notify user | If not found: Log warning, skip notification

**Edge cases**:
- Email exists but user not in this account → no notification (correct behavior)
- Email doesn't exist in Fizzy → log warning, potentially create invite flow later
- Multiple users with same Identity in different accounts → correct account scoping

## Notification Rules

Which events trigger notifications:
- ✅ **beads_issue_assigned**: Notify new assignee
- ✅ **beads_comment_created**: Notify board watchers (excluding comment author)
- ✅ **beads_issue_closed**: Notify board watchers (excluding closer)
- ✅ **beads_issue_reopened**: Notify board watchers
- ✅ **beads_issue_started**: Notify assignee if set
- ❌ **beads_issue_title_changed**: No notification (minor change)
- ❌ **beads_issue_priority_changed**: No notification (minor change)

## Anti-Spam Measures

Reuse Fizzy patterns:
- Exclude creator from notifications (don't notify yourself)
- Email bundling (multiple events → single email per time window)
- Push notification throttling
- In-app notifications collapse by card

## Dependencies
Requires Rich Event Creation epic complete (need semantic events with proper particulars).

## Success Criteria
- Assign beads issue to yourself → receive notification
- Add comment to watched issue → watchers notified
- Email bundling works (multiple events = one email)
- Push notifications contain correct deep links
- In-app notification count updates in real-time

Current implementation only shows when issues are created. Users need to see:

title: Implement change object classes
description:
Create value objects representing semantic changes that encapsulate event creation logic.

## Files to Create

`app/services/beads/changes/comment_addition.rb`

`app/services/beads/changes/priority_change.rb`
`app/services/beads/changes/labels_change.rb`

## Interface Contract
Each change object MUST implement these 4 methods:
```ruby
def event_action          # String: event action name
def event_particulars     # Hash: data for Event.particulars
def actor_email           # String or nil: email of person who made change
def notifiable?           # Boolean: should trigger notifications?
```

## Full Implementations

### StatusChange
```ruby
# app/services/beads/changes/status_change.rb
module Beads
  module Changes
    class StatusChange
      attr_reader :from, :to, :actor

      def initialize(from:, to:, actor: nil)
        @from, @to, @actor = from, to, actor
      end

      def event_action
        case to
        when "closed" then "beads_issue_closed"
        when "open"
          from == "closed" ? "beads_issue_reopened" : "beads_issue_started"
        when "in_progress" then "beads_issue_started"
        when "blocked" then "beads_issue_blocked"
        else "beads_issue_status_changed"
        end
      end

      def event_particulars
        { old_status: from, new_status: to }
      end

      def actor_email
        actor
      end

      def notifiable?
        true
      end
    end
  end
end
```

### AssignmentChange
```ruby
# app/services/beads/changes/assignment_change.rb
module Beads
  module Changes
    class AssignmentChange
      attr_reader :from, :to

      def initialize(from:, to:)
        @from, @to = from, to
      end

      def event_action
        to.present? ? "beads_issue_assigned" : "beads_issue_unassigned"
      end

      def event_particulars
        { old_assignee: from, new_assignee: to }
      end

      def actor_email
        to || from
      end

      def notifiable?
        to.present?  # Notify on assignment, not unassignment
      end
    end
  end
end
```

### CommentAddition
```ruby
# app/services/beads/changes/comment_addition.rb
module Beads
  module Changes
    class CommentAddition
      attr_reader :comment

      def initialize(comment_hash)
        @comment = comment_hash.deep_symbolize_keys
      end

      def event_action
        "beads_comment_created"
      end

      def event_particulars
        {
          comment_author: comment[:author],
          comment_created_at: comment[:created_at],
          comment_excerpt: truncate_comment(comment[:body]),
          comment_body_hash: hash_comment(comment[:body])
        }
      end

      def actor_email
        comment[:author]
      end

      def notifiable?
        true
      end

      private

      def truncate_comment(body)
        body&.slice(0, 200) || ""
      end

      def hash_comment(body)
        Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(body || "")
      end
    end
  end
end
```

title: Backfill state cache for existing beads issues
description:
Populate state cache for issues that exist before the cache system is deployed, enabling change detection for all issues going forward.

## Context
When state cache is first deployed:
- Existing beads issues have no cached state
- First update mutation will have nothing to compare against
- Need strategy to backfill cache

## Two Approaches

### Approach 1: Organic Backfill (Implemented in fizzy-8h3)
BeadsBridge.handle_update already handles missing cache:
```ruby
if state.nil?
  Rails.logger.info("BeadsBridge: No cache for \#{issue.id}, treating as create")
  return handle_create(issue)
end
```

**Pros**: No extra work, happens naturally
**Cons**: Issues with no updates never get cached

### Approach 2: Explicit Backfill (This Task)
Run rake task after deployment to pre-populate cache.

## Implementation

Add to `lib/tasks/beads.rake`:
```ruby
desc "Backfill state cache for all existing beads issues"
task backfill_cache: :environment do
  Board.where.not(repo_path: nil).find_each do |board|
    puts "Backfilling cache for board: \#{board.name}"
    
    begin
      # Fetch all current issues
      client = board.beads_client
      issues_data = fetch_all_issues(client)
      
      issues_data.each do |issue_data|
        issue = BeadsIssue.new(issue_data)
        issue.board = board
        
        # Serialize and cache
        serialized = BeadsBridge.new(board).send(:serialize_issue, issue)
        
        BeadsIssueState.upsert(
          {
            board_id: board.id,
            issue_id: issue.id,
            snapshot: serialized.to_json,
            synced_at: Time.current
          },
          unique_by: [:board_id, :issue_id]
        )
      end
      
      puts "  ✓ Cached \#{issues_data.size} issues"
    rescue BeadsClient::Error => e
      puts "  ✗ Failed: \#{e.message}"
    end
  end
end

def fetch_all_issues(client)
  # Get all issues across all statuses
  all_issues = []
  %w[open in_progress blocked closed].each do |status|
    issues = client.list(status: status, full: true) || []
    all_issues.concat(issues)
  end
  all_issues
end
```

## When to Run

**After deploying state cache**:
```bash
# Migrate database
bin/rails db:migrate

# Backfill existing issues
bin/rails beads:backfill_cache

# Start mutation poller (should already be running)
```

**Not needed if**:
- Brand new Fizzy installation (no existing beads issues)
- Can wait for organic backfill (first update triggers cache)

## Verification

After backfill:
```bash
bin/rails beads:check_cache

# Should show:
# ✓ roboco: 45 cached / 45 actual
# ✓ messenger: 12 cached / 12 actual
# ✓ fizzybeads: 23 cached / 23 actual
```

## Edge Cases

**Issue deleted between list and cache**:
- Upsert handles gracefully (won't error)
- Cache may have stale entry
- Next delete mutation will clean it up

**Board with no issues**:
- No error, just logs "Cached 0 issues"

**Beads daemon not running**:
- Catch BeadsClient::Error
- Log failure, continue to next board

## Alternative: Lazy Backfill
If explicit backfill seems heavy:
- Rely entirely on organic backfill via handle_update
- Issues only cached when they receive update mutations
- Acceptable if most issues get updated eventually

## Recommendation
Run explicit backfill ONCE after deployment for clean state.
Then organic backfill handles any stragglers.

title: Create BeadsIssueEventNotifier class
description:
Implement notifier class that determines who should receive notifications for beads issue events.

## File to Create
`app/models/notifier/beads_issue_event_notifier.rb`

## Implementation
```ruby
class Notifier::BeadsIssueEventNotifier < Notifier
  def recipients
    case event.action
    when "beads_issue_assigned"
      # Notify new assignee (if they exist in Fizzy)
      user = find_user_by_email(event.new_assignee)
      user ? [user] : []

    when "beads_issue_published", "beads_issue_closed", "beads_issue_reopened"
      # Notify board watchers (excluding creator)
      board_watchers_except_creator

    when "beads_comment_created"
      # Notify board watchers (excluding comment author)
      author = find_user_by_email(event.comment_author)
      board_watchers_except(author || event.creator)

    when "beads_issue_started", "beads_issue_blocked"
      # Notify assignee if set
      assignee = find_user_by_email(event.new_assignee || issue.assignee)
      assignee ? [assignee] : []

    else
      []  # No notifications for title/description/priority changes
    end.compact
  end

  private

  def find_user_by_email(email)
    return nil unless email.present?

    identity = Identity.find_by(email_address: email)
    return nil unless identity

    # Find user in current account
    user = identity.users.find_by(account: event.board.account)
    
    unless user
      Rails.logger.warn("BeadsIssueEventNotifier: Email \#{email} not found in account \#{event.board.account.id}")
    end

    user
  end

  def board_watchers_except_creator
    board_watchers_except(event.creator)
  end

  def board_watchers_except(excluded_user)
    event.board.accesses
      .where(role: [:owner, :admin, :member])
      .where.not(user_id: excluded_user&.id)
      .map(&:user)
  end

  def issue
    @issue ||= event.eventable
  end
end
```

## Email Mapping Strategy

Beads → Fizzy user lookup:
1. Extract email from event.particulars (new_assignee, comment_author, etc.)
2. Look up Identity: `Identity.find_by(email_address: email)`
3. Find User in current account: `identity.users.find_by(account: board.account)`
4. If not found: Log warning, return nil (no notification sent)

**Why this works**:
- Identities are global (same email across accounts)
- Users are account-scoped (membership)
- Lookup respects account isolation

**Edge cases handled**:
- Email doesn't exist → nil (logged)
- Email exists but not in this account → nil (correct)
- Multiple users with same Identity across accounts → correct one selected via account scope

## Notification Rules

**Notify assignee**:
- beads_issue_assigned (you've been assigned work)
- beads_issue_started (work you're assigned started)

**Notify board watchers**:
- beads_issue_published (new work on board)
- beads_issue_closed (work completed)
- beads_issue_comment_created (discussion happening)

**No notifications**:
- beads_issue_title_changed (minor edit)
- beads_issue_unassigned (removal, not actionable)

## Testing
Unit tests verifying recipient logic for each action type.

```markdown
### Beads State Cache

BeadsIssueState table caches last known state of each beads issue for change detection.

**Why**: Beads mutation API returns generic 'update', not semantic changes. We cache previous state to compare and detect WHAT changed (status, assignee, comments, etc.).

**Schema**: board_id + issue_id → JSON snapshot + synced_at timestamp

**Lifecycle**:
- Create mutation: Store initial state
- Update mutation: Compare cached state → detect changes → update cache
- Delete mutation: Remove cache entry

**Cache location**: `app/models/beads_issue_state.rb`
**Change detection**: `app/services/beads/change_detector.rb`
**Change objects**: `app/services/beads/changes/*.rb`
```

```markdown
### Beads Event System

Beads events are created by comparing cached state to current state:
- BeadsIssueState table caches previous issue snapshots
- ChangeDetector service identifies semantic changes
- Change objects define event actions and particulars
- BeadsBridge creates events for each meaningful change

**Key insight**: Generic 'update' mutations require state comparison to determine event type.
```

```bash
"
```

Get webhook.site URL:
1. Visit https://webhook.site
2. Copy unique URL
3. Use in webhook creation above

### Test 1: Close Event Webhook
```bash
# Create and close issue
bd create "Webhook close test" --actor hi@fizzybeads.com
sleep 7

bd close fizzy-xxx --actor hi@fizzybeads.com
sleep 7

# Check webhook.site
# Should see POST request with payload:
# {
#   "event": {
#     "action": "beads_issue_closed",
#     "issue": {

#       "title": "Webhook close test",

#     }

```

### Test 2: Comment Event Webhook
```bash
bd create "Webhook comment test"
sleep 7

bd comment fizzy-xxx "Test comment for webhook" --actor hi@fizzybeads.com
sleep 7

# Check webhook.site for comment event payload
```

### Test 3: Assignment Event Webhook
```bash
bd create "Webhook assignment test" --assignee hi@fizzybeads.com
sleep 7

# Check webhook.site for assignment event
```

### Test 4: HMAC Signature Verification
```bash
# Check webhook has signature secret
bin/rails runner "puts Webhook.first.signature_secret"

# In webhook.site, check headers:
# X-Webhook-Signature should be present
# Value should be HMAC-SHA256 of payload

# Verify with:
expected = OpenSSL::HMAC.hexdigest('SHA256', secret, payload)

```

### Test 5: Subscription Filtering

```bash
sleep 7
```

- [ ] Webhook receives beads_issue_closed event
- [ ] Webhook receives beads_comment_created event
- [ ] Webhook receives beads_issue_assigned event
- [ ] Payload includes issue ID, title, status
- [ ] Payload includes old/new values from particulars
- [ ] HMAC signature present and valid
- [ ] Subscription filtering works (only subscribed actions)
- [ ] Delivery happens within 10 seconds of event
